title: The current normal form is controlled across two analytic radii but not at one radius

two_radius_bound.nested_radius_estimate: For 0<sigma<rho, S_sigma<=(1/2)[1+rho^(-2)(1-(sigma/rho)^2)^(-2)]G_rho. Use sqrt(H_nH_(n+1))<=(H_n+H_(n+1))/2 and sum_(m>=1)m q^(m-1)=(1-q)^(-2).
two_radius_bound.modified_energy_control: K1568 implies |sum_n a_n(sigma)M_n|<=C_m|e|||A||_infinity C_(sigma,rho)G_rho and |sum_n a_n(sigma)int A dot partial_t j_n|<=C_m B_A C_(sigma,rho)G_rho.
two_radius_bound.combined_identity: Summing K1563's identity at the inner radius therefore bounds the radial term at the same tier and the differentiated-current term by the outer analytic energy, conditional on finite B_A and G_rho.
two_radius_bound.same_radius_obstruction: No cutoff-independent constant bounds S_rho by G_rho at one radius. Taking only H_N=a_N(rho)^(-1) and H_(N+1)=a_(N+1)(rho)^(-1) nonzero keeps G_rho=2 while the nth cross contribution equals sqrt(N+1)/rho.
two_radius_bound.consequence: The normal form removes the apparent spatial derivative loss and is bankable with an analytic-radius margin, but it does not create a same-radius coercive energy or repair K1450's finite radius loss.
two_radius_bound.scope_guard: This conditional two-radius estimate does not prove global coefficient integrability, positivity of a limiting radius, a gauge-invariant completion, a closed completed-domain modified energy, or cutoff-uniform global flow.
